lawyer:
Abul Basher Bhuiyan with Md Shamsul Alam, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
MU Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State.
parties:
Montu and others ------ Petitioners 
vs 
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Criminal Revision under section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of Montu, Sayeed and Iman Ali are directed against the judgment and order dated 3-8-2004 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail in Criminal Appeal No. 103 of 2004 affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 23-5-2004 passed by the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Tangail, in GR Case No.1 (Druta Bichar) of 2004 corresponding to Tangail PS Case No. 19 dated 24-2-2004 convicting the petitioners under section 4(1) of the Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh (Druta Bichar) 2002 sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 (two) years and to pay a fine of Taka 5,000 each in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 6(six) months more. 

 7. The learned Magistrate on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record convicted the petitioners by the judgment and order dated 23-5-2004 convicting the petitioners under section 4(1) of Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh (Druta Bichar), 2002 sentencing him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2(two) years and to pay a fine of Taka 5,000 in default to suffer simple imprisonment for 6(six) months. 

 8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of conviction dated 23-5- 2004 passed by the learned Magistrate, First Class, Tangail the petitioners as appellants preferred Criminal Appeal No. 103 of 2004 before the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail, who on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record dismissed the appeal and upheld the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the learned trial Court. 

 10. Now we are called upon to consider whether the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail is justified in passing the impugned. judgment and order of conviction and sentence against the accused-petitioners under section 4(1) of Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh (Druta Bichar), 2002 in the light of the evidence on record and submissions of the learned Advocate of the contending parties. 

 11. Mr Abul Basher Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, has placed before me the first information report of the case, charge framed at the trial against the accused-petitioners, evidence of witnesses taken during the trial as well as the impugned judgment. 

 13. Mr Abul Basher Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the petitioners are quite innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case out of enmity or to harass and humiliate the petitioners. He further submits that the courts below failed to consider the facts .of the prosecution case and has miserably failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt; that it is transpired from the evidence of PW 1 that at the time of occurrence he was not present at the place of occurrence; that he lodged the first information report after hearing the occurrence from the victim and from the people who are present at the time of occurrence; that the petitioner No.2 is also a hearsay witness and since he serves in the clinics of the informant and of the victim, as such, out of obligation he deposed before the Court. It is further submitted that PW 3 stated the place of occurrence is at Tangi-Mymensingh road but PW 2 stated that the place of occurrence is Dhaka-Tagnail road; that the PW 4 victim of the case deposed that on 24-2-2004 at about 7-00 AM when he was returning home supplying food to the labourers he was hurt at random from the back side and at one stage he fell in front of the Kechigate and at 2-30 PM he regained his sense but he could not identify anybody; that PW 5 deposed in his cross examination that he could not remember the date of occurrence and, he said nothing against the petitioners; that PW 6 stated in his examination in chief that he had heard about the occurrence from the people and he did not see who hurt his brother and that PW 7 stated that he heard the occurrence from the people and some body had beaten the victim. He further submits that PW 8 is doctor who stated in his examination-in-chief that all the wounds are simple in nature and in other place he said that hurts are grievous in nature and, as such, he deposed self-contradictory statement and that PW 9 is investigating officer of the case who submitted the charge-sheet without proper investigation. It is further stated that learned Magistrate without considering the facts and circumstance of the case and evidence on record passed the impugned judgment on the basis of mere surmise and conjecture and he passed the order of conviction and sentence in an unlawful manner and the court of appeal below also without applying with judicial mind dismissed the appeal confirming the judgment passed by the Magistrate on 23-05-2004. 

 16. The appellate court as last court of fact considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record found the accused- petitioners guilty under section 4(1) of Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh (Druta Bichar), 2002 affirming the judgment and order of the Magistrate dated 23-5-2004. I do like to reinter in the evidence on record as the trial Court as well as the appellate court carefully scrutinised the evidence arrived at a decision. I like to discuss salient features of the evidence on record. 

 25. PW 9 is the investigating officer who visited the place of occurrence, prepared map and index thereof, recorded the evidence of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and being satisfied he submitted charge- sheet against the accused persons. He further deposed that he seized blood-stained lungi and ganji in presence of witnesses Golam Faroque and Bablu. He proved the seizure list marked Exhibit-2 and his signature marked Exhibit 2/2. He further deposed that he saw the PC & PR of the accused persons and found as many as 8 cases under different sections against the accused Montu and 11 (eleven) cases against accused Mamun. 

 26. It must be remembered by all concerned that mere allegations in the first information report against the accused-petitioners that they demanded subscription from the informant Saiful and his nephew Shibli Sadik and on being refused the accused persons being armed with Chinese Axe, Ram Dao, Pistol, etc. attacked Shibli Sadik on 24-2- 2004 at about 7-45 AM and injured him severely and they later on entering into the under-construction building of the informant damaged articles worth Taka 25,000 has no legal value in the eye of law unless such allegations are not established by convincing and credible evidence. 

 28. In the instant case from the evidence of 9 witnesses and the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as the learned Assistant Attorney-General, it transpires that the case has been proved that the informant and his nephew managed Seba Clinic located to the east side of old bus stand, and it has further been proved that the nephew of the informant was seriously injured and the clinic was damaged by the petitioners. The vital question is, who caused him injuries and damaged the clinic. It is crystal clear from the consistent evidence of PWs that the accused persons being armed with pistol, Chinese Axe, Ramdao, Kirich attacked nephew of the informant on 24-2-2004 at about 7-45 AM. Further it appears from the evidence on record the accused persons demanded subscription from the informant and from his nephew Shibli Sadik and the accused- petitioners very unlawfully created terror and panic in the area and later on they also attacked the nephew of the informant on the date of occurrence causing him serious injuries. 

 31. In the light of explanation of the above section 2 of Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh (Druta Bichar) Ain, 2002, I am of the opinion that the facts and circumstances and evidence on record of this case clearly shows that the accused- petitioners demanded subscription from the informant Saiful Islam and from his nephew Shibli Sadik, and his nephew victim Shibli Sadik who on his refusal to pay the amount demanded by the accused-petitioners who created terror and panic being armed with deadly weapons and attacked Shibli Sadik on 24-2-2004 and injured him mercilessly for which Shibli Sadik had to go under treatment in Tangail Sadar Hospital and the doctor examining him opined that his injuries were grievous in nature and his blood-stained lungi and ganji were also seized through seizure list which was identified by the witnesses and the same were also marked material exhibit. 

 32. From the evidence discussed above it is found that the accused-petitioner Montu against whom 8 (eight) cases under different sections are pending who along with his associates, Sayeed and Iman Ali and others created terror and panic in the place of occurrence and assaulted the nephew of the informant victim Shibli Sadik mercilessly in order to get illegal subscription from them. These activities of the accused-petitioners clearly fall under definition of Ain Sringkhola Bignokari Aparadh. 

 33. All the witnesses corroborated the prosecution case in all material particulars. There is nothing on record to disbelieve the convincing and corroborative evidence of the competent witnesses, having no reasons whatsoever to depose falsely against the accused-petitioners. 

 36. Defence version is that Bablu is the employee of Seba Clinic whose evidence cannot be believed. In this respect I am of the view that the evidence of Bablu of the concerned clinic cannot be rejected merely on the ground that he was working under the informant. Credibility of a witness is accepted if it is corroborated by the evidence of other witnesses but credibility should be tested in the touch stone of the broad probabilities of the case. In this case this witness is a most natural witness in whose presence the occurrence took place and other independent witnesses corroborated his evidence. 

 37. PW 3 Jamila Khatoon is the eye-witness of the occurrence who deposed that the accused Montu dealt a chinese axe blow and she saw a pistol in the hand of accused Alam, a ramdao in the hand of accused Iman Ali and chinese axe in the hand of Sayed. She further deposed that the accused persons also damaged Seba Clinic. Conviction of the accused person cannot depend on the number of witnesses but quality of witnesses. Conviction can be based on the evidence of a single evidence if it is found reliable and trustworthy. The direct evidence of PW 3 which is in general agreement as to material circumstances is sufficient enough to convict the accused-petitioners. 

 38. Both the trial Court and the appellate Court concurrently found the accused-petitioners guilty in the light of the evidence on record. It is well settled that the revisional court does not interfere with the concurrent findings of fact save in exceptional circumstances as when a question of law of general public importance arises or a decision shocks the conscience of the court. This court has the enormous power to interfere even with findings of facts making no distinction between judgment of acquittal and conviction if this Court finds that the appellate court has acted perversely or otherwise improperly. But on perusal of the evidence on record, I find that the impugned judgment is well reasoned and well founded and there is no reason to interfere with the concurrent findings of both the courts below. 

 39. Having given my best consideration to the materials on record and after hearing the learned Advocates of both sides, I hold that the judgment and order dated 3-8-04 is based on evidence on record and his judgment is well reasoned and the impugned judgment is not vitiated by any misreading and non-reading of evidence and the judgment and order dated 3-8-2004 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 103 of 2004 affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 23-5-04 passed by the learned. Magistrate, First Class, Tangail in GR case No. 1 (Druta Bichar) of 2004 is quite justified which should not call for any interference.
